name: Vikran Engineering Ltd
title: Vikran Engineering Ltd - 544496 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Vikran is an EPC contractor pivoting to solar, with FY26 revenue of INR1,249 crore and EBITDA margin near 14%, while operating cash flow stays negative and receivables reached about INR1,000 crore.

summary.headline: Vikran FY26 revenue hit a record INR1,249 crore (vs INR916 crore) with EBITDA margin near 14%; FY27 guided at INR2,200 crore plus.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR647 crore, up from INR355 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA of INR92 crore (14.2% margin) and PAT of INR56 crore (vs INR38 crore). For FY26, revenue rose to INR1,249 crore, EBITDA was about INR175 crore (around 14%) and PAT was INR92 crore (vs about INR78 crore). Management attributed margin dilution to delayed Jal Jeevan Mission receivables (provisioned, mostly in Q4), and to early-stage solar EPC projects. The company closed its acquisition of NOPL Solar (969 MW PM-KUSUM project) at end-April 2026 and guided FY27 revenue of INR2,200 crore plus, with a 14-15% EBITDA margin target.

financial_highlights.value: upgraded to IND A, stable outlook

segments.name: Power T&D
segments.commentary: Management sees FY27 power T&D at about 30% of revenue, focused on selective 765 kV GIS/AIS projects for clients such as Power Grid and NTPC. Scope includes substations, lines, underground cabling and smart metering.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Solar is now the main growth pillar, with management expecting about 60% of FY27 revenue. Marquee wins include 100 MW AC (Ellume Energy), 400 MW AC / 580 MWp DC (NTPC Renewable) and 600 MW (NOPL Solar); 20 MW of NOPL is commissioned, with more due by end-May.

segments.name: Water infrastructure
segments.commentary: Water is about 10% of FY27 revenue from the existing order book, roughly INR600 crore; no new water bids for about 18 months. Jal Jeevan Mission receivables are about INR400 crore, and INR17-18 crore was received in FY27 to date.

segments.name: NOPL Solar (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Acquired 100% at end-April 2026; project cost INR4,200 crore with sanctioned lender funding. Management cites revenue over INR500 crore over 25 years, 85-88% EBITDA margin, and about INR1 crore per month from the first 20 MW.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue from operations guided at INR2,200 crore plus (CFO also cited INR2,200-2,500 crore), with or without NOPL, per management.
EBITDA margin guided at 14-15% for FY27, which management said it was confident of maintaining.
Possible additional INR1,000-1,400 crore solar EPC order from the Onix balance EPC scope, not yet in the INR5,700 crore order book; may be booked at arm's length price.
FY27 growth expected to be higher than FY26; FY28 revenue about INR3,000 crore plus; management declined to give FY29 figures.
Operating cash flow expected to turn positive from FY28; management said no further equity dilution is planned.
Data centre EPC target of about INR100 crore order book in FY27, initially 50-100 MW.
MNRE and MSEDCL have extended the NOPL project deadline to March 2027.
capex_capacity: NOPL 969 MW PM-KUSUM project: 148 MW in advanced execution; about 85% of land identified since takeover; about 150 locations; 20 MW commissioned, with 20 MW more due in days.
Project funding of INR4,200 crore is sanctioned by a major lender, and the existing financing line rolls over to the new owner subject to a promoter evaluation; backup financing is in place.
Solar EPC: 500 MW EPC project in execution; company's total under-construction portfolio stated as about 1.5 GW (1 GW developer, 500 MW EPC).
Operational footprint: 22 states, 190 locations, about 1,200 staff, with about 222 at the Thane head office.
Management is cautiously evaluating Middle East and Africa opportunities, and says it is not pursuing a developer or investment model for data centres.
demand_pricing: Government push and private demand for solar; management sees better cash flow and margins in solar.
Management said it is selectively bidding; no new water orders for about 18 months.
Management said the company has no BESS in its current scope but has bid for some BESS projects.
Supply chain is largely dependent on China, but management says procurement was front-loaded in FY26 and the West Asia conflict has had limited impact so far.
Management says CFO-level margin for FY23-25 was 15-17%, and that projects are being chosen for similar margin range.

qa_highlights.question: Will EBITDA margin recover from 13-14% to historical 18-22%, and what is the status of the Onix project and its financing?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said FY23-25 EBITDA was 15-17%, with FY26 at about 14% due to JJM receivable provisions (reversed on collection). Management said the Onix SPV is now 100% owned; the lender is comfortable, and 4 projects are commissioned with 2 more due by end-May.

qa_highlights.question: What is execution in FY27 with and without NOPL, and what milestones have been achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management says INR2,200 crore plus is achievable with or without NOPL, and that a plan without NOPL 'does not make a lot of sense'. Milestones since the April takeover are limited to a few commissioned projects; land and evacuation issues are cleared.

qa_highlights.question: How much receivables exposure is there from water/JJM, and how much was provided in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said about INR400 crore of water receivables are due from JJM. About INR20 crore of provision was taken in FY26, mostly in Q4; the CFO said there is no specific high-risk receivable.

qa_highlights.question: When will cash flow turn positive, and will there be equity dilution?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said there are no plans for further equity dilution and that operating cash flow is expected to turn positive from FY28; the order book has grown from about INR2,000 crore to over INR5,000 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue mix for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said about 60% solar, 30% power T&D and about 10% water.

qa_highlights.question: Is the additional INR1,400 crore NOPL solar order included in the INR5,700 crore order book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not included because the order is not yet placed and documentation is pending; the CFO said about INR1,000 crore may be booked in coming days, executable over 12-15 months.

risks_watch: Working capital: payables up about 60% to INR788 crore and receivables about INR1,000 crore; operating cash flow remains negative.
Government JJM receivables: about INR400 crore, with a shortfall in one or two states; provisions to be reversed on collection.
NOPL execution: about 85% land identified, 150-odd locations to complete by March 2027 deadline; the lender line roll-over is subject to a promoter evaluation.
Pending INR1,000-1,400 crore Onix balance EPC order (arm's length pricing) that would be additional to the INR5,700 crore order book.
Supply-chain and geopolitical risk from China sourcing and the West Asia conflict; management is hedging with large suppliers.
Data centre EPC entry, with a small INR100 crore target; no formal order yet.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY27 revenue and margin guidance, but cautious and occasionally evasive on receivables, cash flow and the Onix/NOPL details. Management gave specific numbers when asked about FY27 mix, while its answers on FY29 and the Onix order book were less precise. Several figures were corrected mid-call (NOPL monthly revenue, water receivables).
key_quotes: So, considering our financial strength, we are already an A-rated company, whereas, Onix was, I believe, a BB or a BBB rated.
14% -15% is where we are very confident on and hoping to maintain that.
Three years would be a long unrealistic expectation for us to provide actual figures on with, you know, backing from data.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR2,200 crore plus (vs INR1,249 crore in FY26, about 76% growth), backed by a INR5,700 crore order book, 1 GW NOPL project with 20 MW commissioned, and a 500 MW EPC project in execution; order-book conversion timing and NOPL ramp are not fully quantified.
